L4-L6 CONSTRAINT/LIGHTS-OUT mechanic (2026-07-11, claude-fable-5, independently re-verified by the outer loop on both level-counter and game_state signals): PREDICATE cells display a 3x3 ring pattern around their center where each ring position means: black(0) = that neighbor must MATCH the predicate's center color; '2' = must DIFFER; '3' = no constraint (out-of-board or another predicate). A top-right legend column lists the level's color cycle; clicking a plain cell cycles it one step. Starting at L5, FLIPPER cells appear: clicking one flips itself plus whichever neighbors are indicated by small marks drawn INSIDE the cell -- the mark positions are a literal diagram of the flip mask (L5: a centered cross = flips all 4 orthogonal neighbors; L6's finale: every cell is a flipper, but the mark sits top-center = flips self + NORTH only, not the L5 cross -- READ the mark, never assume the previous level's mask transfers). Flips onto predicate cells or off-board simply vanish (predicates never change). Multi-flipper levels are GF(2) LINEAR SYSTEMS -- solve with Gaussian elimination, not greedy clicking. A wrong flip-model batch is recoverable without a reset: the mismatch pattern between predicted and actual post-click state uniquely identifies the true mask, letting a correct re-solve proceed from the live state (this is exactly how L6 was won, after an initial 11-click batch assumed the wrong mask and produced 9 mismatches).
